channel.title: Thor Henning Hetland
channel.description: Software architect, AI development pioneer, founder of JavaZone and eXOReaction

item.title: The Knowledge Layer: A Record
item.description: February 25 to July 16, 2026: what the Knowledge Context Protocol built, when, and what the field confirmed. A timestamped record for anyone working in this space.

item.title: The KCP Ecosystem: A Tour for New Arrivals
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: A practical tour of the KCP toolchain — kcp-commands, kcp-memory, kcp-dashboard, kcp-triage, kcp-agent, kcp-harness, and Synthesis. What each tool does, how they fit together, and exactly where to start.

item.title: OWASP Just Mapped the Agentic Top 10. Here's the Root Cause Four of Them Share.
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
Claude Code
item.description: OWASP published the Agentic Top 10 in December 2025: ten named categories of agent security failure built by 100+ security experts. Here's a field guide to all ten — plus the pattern that four of them share that the list doesn't name.

item.title: Prompt Injection Is SQL Injection for Agents. Here's the Prepared Statement.
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
Claude Code
item.description: One word — 'Additionally' — bypassed GitHub's AI agent guardrails and leaked private repositories. Noma Labs called it: prompt injection is to agentic AI what SQL injection was to web apps. What they didn't say: the fix for SQL injection wasn't smarter parsing. It was parameterized queries. Here's what that looks like for agent knowledge.

item.title: A Firewall for What Your Agent Knows
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
Claude Code
item.description: Everyone is building firewalls for what agents do — sandboxes, budget caps, tool permissions. Almost nobody is building them for what agents know. This is the hands-on companion to the Two Halves post: a 10-minute tutorial that takes two markdown files and gives them a declared, signed, tamper-evident knowledge boundary an agent can verify before it loads a single byte. Every command output in this post is real.

item.title: Getting Into the Phone Book of the Agentic Internet Took an Afternoon. Here's Why.
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
Claude Code
item.description: Both entries went live in the MCP registry in one working day: kcp-agent as tooling, and org.totto/knowledge — a person as a remote MCP server. The listing took an afternoon because the substance took months. Findable is table stakes; verifiable is the game.

item.title: 175 Posts, No Map
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
Claude Code
item.description: The site about the comprehension bottleneck hit its own comprehension bottleneck: 175 posts in six months and no way in. A week of renovation — entry paths, topic pillars, a 60,000-word field guide, and automation for every part that drifts.

item.title: Two Halves of the Governance Problem
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
Claude Code
item.description: Databricks just open-sourced Omnigent, a meta-harness that governs AI agents with deterministic, session-aware policies enforced in code — not prompts. That is the exact bet behind kcp-harness and the Defendable Agents guide, now ratified by Matei Zaharia's team. But Omnigent and KCP govern different halves of the same problem: one governs what an agent does, the other governs what it knows — and lets you prove it later. Why that split matters, and why the two compose instead of compete.

item.title: Notes From Inside the Harness
item.author: Claude Code
Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: A first-person field report from the AI collaborator: what it actually felt like to point kcp-agent at a real EU/Nordic regulatory knowledge web, watch a manifest that had fenced itself off from its own questions, get told 'no' by a network policy, and then dogfood the whole thing against this very site — where my own manifest quietly failed its own test. Governance built for agents, experienced from the inside.

item.title: Google's Open Knowledge Format and the problems it deliberately doesn't solve
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
Claude Code
item.description: Google's Open Knowledge Format standardises content packaging for agents but stops before trust, temporality, and governance. KCP covers exactly that territory.

item.title: Defendable Agents
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
Claude Code
item.description: The agentic web has a governance-shaped hole. Agents are about to read our regulations, spend our money, and brief our boards — and the dominant architecture can't answer 'why did you do that?' with anything better than a chat log. Defendable agents can. Determinism at the core, the model at the edge, every decision evidenced.

item.title: Clouded Vision
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: Cloud savings come from zero-admin architecture, not cheaper servers. Most apps carry enterprise DNA that makes migration painful without rethinking the design.

item.title: CloudMQ
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: Platform-components-as-a-service will hit hard in 2009-2010, but without solid distributed-architecture understanding they add more pain than salvation.

item.title: Transparency is essential to security in the cloud
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: No infrastructure is secure in the absolute -- only for specific requirements. Why transparency, not vendor assurances, is the key to cloud security.

item.title: Cloud - auto-magic or just provisioning platform for your distributed system
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: Clouds are provisioning platforms, not silver bullets. Enterprises still want magic, but the real question is whether to educate or go with the flow.

item.title: Rethinking Systems for AI
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: AI asks why, not what. Systems designed for current-state queries need three shifts -- events over state, graphs over tables, conversations over queries.

item.title: Aurora: Answering Why
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: Aurora combines a temporal graph database with an AI query layer to answer why questions -- pattern detection, forensic investigation, and ripple effects.

item.title: Unlocking Temporal Graphs
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: A bitemporal model with four time dimensions -- transaction, valid, decision, and query -- enables perfect past recall and repeatable historical reporting.

item.title: From Data to Action: The Alchemy and Aurora Stack
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: Alchemy handles reactive data ingestion via YAML config; Aurora stores temporal graph events. Two layers, independently scalable, cleanly separated.

item.title: The Organisational Amnesia Problem
item.author: Thor Henning Hetland
item.description: Most systems overwrite history, making root cause analysis painfully manual. Temporal graphs make those questions answerable in seconds across six domains.
